newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Rebound after hitting bottom.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Rebound after hitting bottom.

text.p: Singapore gas oil market retraced some of its earlier losses, rebounding after hitting the lowest levels in a year, brokers said on Wednesday.
A spate of offers for jet and gas oil cargoes came in late Asian trading day and levels were higher than expected.
There was a dearth of bids.

Majors were offering between $23.50-$23.70 for end June to mid July loading gas oil supplies against a bid from a local trader at $23.20 for early July supplies. This compares with the lowest trade done on Tuesday at $22.90.
Jet cargoes were offered in a similar price range between $23.40-$23.70. But there were no takers. Jet was traded at $22.40 for end June supplies and at $23.50 for early July cargoes on Tuesday.
Traders said the rapid rise in levels were "unreal". They said prices are reacting to higher crude levels and talk that the market has bottomed out.
"The market is still well-supplied," said one major. "It'll be interesting to see if the gains would be sustained".
A buy tender from Sri Lanka for early July supplies spurred recovery, one trader said.
Sri Lanka has tendered to buy 250,000 barrels of gasoil and 50,000 barrels of jet for July 12-13 delivery. The company is expected to award its tender to buy end June supplies on Thursday.
Taiwan has also awarded its tender to sell July 2-19 diesel to a local trader at above $22.50.
Demand from China were sporadic. Enquiries were heard at $182 per tonne for July cargoes.
